subject: 7A2DA22B0196E4813CDC85DB1C970313
introduction: These prayers ask to be kept: firm in belief, constant in love, unshaken by tests, and faithful to the Covenant after the passing of its Author. They do not treat steadfastness as an achievement. “Keep me steadfast”, they say, and “protect me from violent tests”. Jesus prayed for Peter “that thy faith fail not” and for the disciples that the Father would “keep” them; a father in the Gospels prayed, “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief”. Peter’s denial, after his confident promise, is the story that explains why steadfastness is prayed for and not presumed.
questions: Why ask God for steadfastness, if being steadfast is something a person does?
The first prayer asks to be protected from “violent tests”. Is it faithless to pray to be spared?
What has Peter’s denial to teach someone who feels entirely firm?

outside.why: Protect me from violent tests. The Lord’s Prayer asks the same: lead us not into temptation.
Keep me steadfast and make me firm. Be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.
Praise for what has been bestowed. The rain descended, and the floods came, and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
Acknowledging Thy unity and confessing. Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
A servant who has believed and is assured. I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
By Thy First Light and Thy Last Manifestation. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.
Make it firm in Your religion. He shall not be afraid of evil tidings: his heart is fixed, trusting in the Lord.
Servants who have hastened to the shade of the Covenant. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one.
Guides to Thy Cause, poor in Thy land. Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
Make firm the feet of Thy loved ones. Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
Peter had said, though all should deny thee, yet will not I; and he went out, and wept bitterly. These prayers never promise steadfastness; they ask for it. What is the difference?

shortfall: The hundred prayers ask for firmness in the Covenant in closely similar words; companions were set to the first stretch only.
